feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear positioning for senior digital communications roles and credible progression within one organization. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition, and tighter structure across overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility: long tenure at NACo with promotions, large-scale website migration, analytics stack ownership, and studio build-out all signal real responsibility.  
- Writing is generally polished and readable, with strong action verbs and relevant technical/detail balance for this field.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); “cross-channel” vs “Multi-channel” is a minor style inconsistency. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies/skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Add one distinctive qualifier tied to the experience section, such as public-sector/member association, advocacy, or enterprise web modernization.
- Reduce list-like channel wording; emphasize outcomes and leadership scope instead of repeating skills listed elsewhere.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, editorial workflows, and digital systems that enable coordinated, organization-wide communications. Skilled at stakeholder alignment and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also appear elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize for consistency: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership strengths over task-level items; e.g., move from “Web & CMS administration” to “Web platform strategy & governance.”
- Consider a sharper version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform strategy & CMS governance • Editorial workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- If space allows, replace one generic item with a more current differentiator such as “AI-enabled search & content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats the header and Soft Skills almost directly.
- “Digital strategy,” “editorial workflow,” “analytics,” and “multimedia” are already covered in more detail under Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest/highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery as an external consultant.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet on improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Emphasize consultant-specific impact: strategy, architecture, governance, and delivery oversight; reduce lower-level phrasing like “technical troubleshooting.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, publishing efficiency gains, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal microsites,” “analytics,” “governance,” and “AI-enabled search” are already echoed in the footer projects and earlier NACo roles; avoid repeating implementation detail here.
- CMS/front-end execution may undersell this recent role if the prior Director role already establishes hands-on platform leadership.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if channel oversight emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and enterprise change rather than broad responsibilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the first sentence with a tighter leadership summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel impact more specific if possible: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rates, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine operations/governance bullets into one concise enterprise-systems point: “Built analytics and publishing infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video-program growth overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity.
- Governance/editorial coordination also appears in adjacent NACo roles; emphasize enterprise ownership here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed at this level: ownership of day-to-day operations, newsletter scale, and launch/growth of recurring advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: managed four weekly newsletters; produced/scaled weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications/advocacy/program teams; improved publishing workflows.
- Add metrics where possible: open/click rates, video views, production cadence, turnaround time, stakeholder groups served, or workflow efficiency gains.
- Use stronger verbs: “managed,” “launched,” “scaled,” “standardized,” “coordinated,” “streamlined” instead of “helped.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; frame this here as scaling/operationalizing, not originating.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this version tactical and execution-focused.

- Rewrite as: Drupal (primary; enterprise/public-sector sites, migrations, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”
- Order by relevance/modernity: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS • jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since the CV already emphasizes workflow architecture elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around automation and operational coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance to the rest of the CV: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Microsoft Teams • Slack • Trello • Basecamp”
- If accurate, add light functional grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team coordination: Teams, Slack”
- If these tools were used to build systems, consider replacing 1–2 names with capability phrasing: “Airtable-based workflow systems • Power Automate and Zapier automations • Jira/Asana project operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same wording verbatim.
- Slack/Teams overlap with general workplace tools; keep them only if they were central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal platform administration and campaign execution without repeating broader “multi-channel communications” claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Expand from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — email campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation, and engagement workflows**
- If accurate, add scale or ownership language tied to recent work: **enterprise/member communications**, **newsletter distribution**, or **journey/campaign setup**
- Keep only the strongest/current platforms; list in order of recency/relevance, likely **Dynamics 365, Higher Logic, Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating audience scale here (“tens of thousands”) since that already appears in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies; use this line to emphasize systems/platforms, not strategy.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer

items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “coordinated daily work with a digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow efficiencies.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on helping launch the team and executing content.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social oversight language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the policy/research support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and program content development.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of multimedia assets produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research coordination + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating leadership in digital operations here, since that growth is already shown in 2015–2024 roles.
